https://cointelegraph.com/news/polish-pr.text: Written by Nate Kostar staff writer Reviewed by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Nate Kostar staff writer Reviewed by Robert Lakin staff editor Polish prosecutors charge suspect in Zondacrypto probe, seek pretrial detention Latest News Published Sep 7, 2026 Polish prosecutors charged Romana Ż. with organized crime and misappropriation offenses involving $2.1 million in Zondacrypto user funds. Polish prosecutors investigating cryptocurrency exchange Zondacrypto, have formally charged an individual, identified as Romana Ż., with participating in an organized criminal group and allegedly misappropriating 7.8 million zlotys ($2.1 million) in user funds. Prosecutors also asked the Katowice-Wschód District Court to place the suspect in pretrial detention, citing concerns that he could flee or interfere with the investigation, according to an official announcement on Monday. Romana Ż. was detained on Sept. 5 over concerns they might flee and was subsequently questioned by prosecutors. The suspect denied the charges and provided a statement, according to Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office. Prosecutors allege Romana Ż. acted with others to misappropriate funds entrusted to the exchange by making unauthorized changes to computer records and interfering with the processing and transmission of exchange data. The charges come after three others detained on Sept. 2 were charged in the investigation over allegations including money laundering, misappropriation of company assets and participation in an organized criminal group. A Polish court ordered all three held in pretrial detention for up to three months. As Cointelegraph previously reported, prosecutors estimated losses connected to Zondacrypto at no less than 350 million zlotys. The investigation was also merged in July with a probe into the 2022 disappearance of Sylwester Suszek, the founder of BitBay, which was later renamed Zondacrypto. Zondacrypto’s Estonian operator, BB Trade Estonia, was declared bankrupt in August, with its first creditors’ meeting scheduled for Sept. 17. Germany: Supporters rally in Hamburg as trial opens over Nord Stream pipeline blasts Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 14/10/2026 - 15:42 GMT+2 Supporters waving Ukrainian flags gathered outside a court in Hamburg on Wednesday, 14 October, in solidarity with a former Ukrainian army officer accused of involvement in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions in the Baltic Sea. … More The demonstration took place outside the Hanseatic Higher Regional Court as the trial opened under tight security. Protesters held signs declaring “Russia is a Terrorist” and challenged the decision to bring war crimes charges. One placard drew a distinction between damaging a gas pipeline and bombing buildings or killing civilians. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Ivan Kuritsyn , from Citizens’ Initiative Vilni De Ua, a non-profit organisation set up by Ukrainians displaced by the war, said the demonstrators had come to show their solidarity with Serhii Kuznietsov . The 50-year-old defendant, identified by German prosecutors as Serhii K. , is accused of helping organise the operation that damaged Nord Stream 1 and 2 on 26 September 2022. Prosecutors allege that he led a team of divers, a boat captain and an explosives expert. He faces several charges, including offences linked to the explosions, property damage, disruption of public services and an alleged war crime involving civilian infrastructure. He has not been convicted. The pipelines were designed to carry Russian gas to Germany. The trial is expected to run for several months, with hearings scheduled until February. https://www.dw.com/en/bulgaria-seeks-sus.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5ORMf Separate sabotage attempts took aim at Starlink facilities in Poland and Bulgaria within a matter of weeks Image: Rafapress/Depositphotos/IMAGO Advertisement Bulgaria on Monday issued European arrest warrants against two 19-year-old German nationals, saying it suspected their involvement in the sabotage of a series of Starlink antennas near the capital Sofia. "The evidence gathered makes it possible to conclude that there are reasonable grounds to suspect the involvement of the two defendants," the court in Sofia rules, granting a request from prosecutors. Ukraine 's military uses Starlink's military-grade satellite internet service Starshield for battlefield communications amid Russia's invasion . Bulgaria does not directly border Ukraine, but it is on the Black Sea , one of the flashpoints of the conflict. A similar case in Poland, which does directly border Ukraine, led to a total of four arrests last week , also in Germany. What do we know about the incident in Bulgaria? The two teenage suspects are accused of deliberately setting fire to the antennas on the evening of October 9. Of 18 in a mountainous region south of Sofia, three were destroyed entirely, two were partially burned and three more were damaged, according to prosecutors. Prosecutors say the suspects entered from Serbia in a car with German license plates, claiming to be tourists, staying just a few hours around the time of the alleged crime. Plamen Tonchev, the head of Bulgaria's domestic intelligence agency DANS, said he was working on the assumption that it was deliberate sabotage and said other such acts could not be ruled out in future. What is the potential tie-in to a Polish sabotage case? News of the arrests follow just a week after a total of four people were arrested in Germany, accused of sabotaging a Starlink satellite communications station in central Poland in late September. German police detained three resident men and a woman, two of them Turkish nationals , early last week. Polish officials said they believed that Russia was behind the sabotage attempt, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk calling it an act of "hybrid warfare." The domestic intelligence agency also claimed that Russia had cooperated with organized crime elements in Germany on the alleged operation. Meanwhile, in the Baltic, Lithuania's prime minister on Sunday said that Russia was likely behind an attempted arson attack on a company hosting communication hardware for Starlink satellites.
